clue.text: Add to trade union quietly

parts.note: taken as written
P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A note on joining a union while keeping one's head down.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is a phrasal verb meaning to total a column of figures, a synonym of add.

clue.text: Habitual drinker, extremely plump, interrupting roof worker?

indicators.note: the end letters break into the middle of the roof worker

parts.note: a tiler lays roof tiles

indicators.note: extremely means the very ends of the word plump

parts.note: first and last letters P and P

explanation.surface: A heavy-drinking, rather plump roofer getting in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippler is someone who regularly drinks alcohol, a habitual boozer.

clue.text: Scout sat back taking in fast snooker player

indicators.note: the reversed word takes in the fasting season
back means the word sat is read in reverse

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
a potter is a player who pots balls

explanation.surface: A talent scout sat back watching a quick snooker player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like an adjective for the player, but it is the noun: the Christian season of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout searches for promising performers or athletes, which is what this person does.

clue.text: Kitty to stream revolutionary Irish medley

parts.note: a pot is a kitty, a shared fund of money
to pour is to stream or flow

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the abbreviation is reversed

explanation.surface: A rebel Irishman's mixture of a cash pot and flowing liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri means a miscellaneous mixture, such as a medley of tunes.

clue.text: Beer found around South Africa game generally

indicators.note: the beer is found surrounding the next letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
RU is rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: A beer drunk around a South African sports match, as is the usual habit.
explanation.walkthrough: RU stands for rugby union, a common crossword 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or in most cases, an idiom equivalent to generally.

clue.text: Worker catching infectious disease not present

indicators.note: the worker catches, holding inside it, the disease

parts.note: an ant is the crossword worker, as in worker ant
BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: An employee off sick after catching something.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means away or missing, so not present at a place.

clue.text: In the morning, power electronic device

parts.note: am (ante meridiem) means in the morning
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Switching on electronic gear early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: An amp is short for amplifier, a piece of audio equipment boosting signals.

clue.text: Subordinate to exploit timber work by Thomas

parts.note: under means subordinate to
to milk is to exploit
wood is timber

explanation.surface: A junior employee told to exploit the lumber, with Thomas mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas is Dylan Thomas, the Welsh poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Under Milk Wood is Dylan Thomas's famous radio play set in a Welsh village.

clue.text: Idyllic garden some enjoyed enormously

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lovely garden that a few people thoroughly liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical paradise, the archetype of a perfect garden.

clue.text: Illustrations involving one system of exercise

indicators.note: the illustrations involve, that is contain, the numeral for one

parts.note: plates are full-page illustrations in a book
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A picture book showing a single fitness routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a named regime of body-conditioning workouts focused on core strength.

clue.text: Army chaplain dwelling with Royal Engineers

parts.note: a pad is informal for one's home or flat
RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A military clergyman lodging alongside an engineering regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the forces' informal title for a clergyman serving with soldiers.

clue.text: Former president's welcome concerning East Midlands area

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was a US president; with the possessive, LINCOLNS
hi is a word of welcome
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A past president's greeting about a region of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East' looks like a piece of wordplay but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincolnshire is an English county lying in the East Midlands region.

clue.text: Line of verse confused three receiving test

indicators.note: the jumbled letters receive the test word inside them
confused tells us the letters of three are jumbled

parts.note: an exam is a test

explanation.surface: Three pupils muddled by a poetry test.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexameter is a line of poetry with six metrical feet, as in Homer.

clue.text: Again arrange holiday location

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a place people go on vacation

explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SORT for the first sense; the second is the ordinary noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word splits into re plus sort for rearranging, and also names a seaside or ski destination.

clue.text: Cut out bodily exertion without hesitation

indicators.note: without signals the hesitation sound is dropped from the exertion word

parts.note: exercise is physical exertion
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Advice to drop physical exertion without dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to remove surgically or delete, the same as cut out.

clue.text: At an initial stage, organ only played

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

indicators.note: played signals the letters of only are rearranged

explanation.surface: Near the start, the church organ was all that was played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests music, but it is the body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Early on means in the first part of a process, soon after the beginning.

clue.text: Fruit, at end of day, marked with blotches

indicators.note: the fruit is placed at the end of the day letter

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Fruit that has gone spotty by the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapple, as in a dapple-grey horse, means spotted or mottled with patches.

clue.text: Big punch around lido mixed for tourist

indicators.note: the punch word goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a haymaker is a powerful swinging punch

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of lido are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fight breaking out at an open-air swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public outdoor swimming pool; a haymaker is a wild, swinging blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A holidaymaker is someone on vacation, a visitor to a place much like a tourist.

clue.text: Dining room repeatedly gutted more seabass

indicators.note: gutted twice means both following words lose their insides, keeping only the end letters

parts.note: outer letters M and E
outer letters S and S

explanation.surface: Gutting fish after fish, more sea bass every time.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a room where military personnel eat together.

clue.text: Uncle Sam's heart lacking constant record

indicators.note: lacking means the constant's letter is taken away

parts.note: the American spelling of centre, so heart in Uncle Sam's English
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: America's core is said to lack a steady record.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam stands for the USA, so his word for heart uses the US spelling CENTER.

clue.text: Greek character's rank discussed

indicators.note: discussed means spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like the rank word

parts.note: a row is a rank, a line of people or things

explanation.surface: A Greek person's rank being talked over.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet, written like a P.

clue.text: Carrier of mine, from rubbish place, about twenty-five pounds

indicators.note: about signals the dump word is turned round

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A cargo of rubbish carried from the dump for a small fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrier of mine' reads as possessive but means something that carries loads in a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit ponies were small horses used underground to haul coal tubs, so a carrier in a mine.

clue.text: At edges, synthetic jumper, for example, recalled famous miser

indicators.note: only the edge letters of synthetic are used

parts.note: outer letters S and C
a roo, kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are taken in reverse

explanation.surface: A jumper made of man-made fibre being returned, recalling a famously tight-fisted man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge, from Dickens's A Christmas Carol, is literature's best-known skinflint.

clue.text: He sculpted bar at home

parts.note: a rod is a bar
in means at home

explanation.surface: A sculptor who shaped a metal bar in his own house.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French artist behind The Thinker, so the man who carved statues.
